headline: Dry through Wednesday morning, then a string of wet, windy storms from Friday brings lowland rain, mountain snow and possible outages.
summary: Dry weather continues into Wednesday morning. A weak front then brings lowland rain Wednesday evening into Thursday, with locally breezy winds from around Whidbey Island northward. Thursday afternoon should be mostly dry in the lowlands, with rain or drizzle lingering in the mountains, and highs stay in the mid to upper 50s through Thursday. The weather turns more active Friday as a series of fronts (the leading edges of storm systems) crosses western Washington. The first brings rain and gusty south winds, strongest along the immediate coast and from Admiralty Inlet northward, where forecasters give 40 to 80% odds of gusts over 40 mph and are watching whether a wind alert will be needed. A warm front keeps rain going at times Saturday on the Olympic Peninsula and near the Canadian border, with a brief drier spell for some of Puget Sound. A cold front follows Saturday night into Sunday with more rain and breezy winds. Because many trees still have leaves, localized power outages are possible over the weekend. Snow levels stay high, mainly 5000 to 8000 feet from Friday into Sunday, so snow falls only at high elevations. Seas near the coast build toward 15 to 20 feet on Friday, and forecasters are watching for high surf. Computer model ensembles (sets of forecast runs) suggest a brief break in the heavier precipitation Sunday night into Monday, followed by another front late Monday and a continued active pattern next week, though that timing is uncertain. River flooding is not expected in the next seven days, but repeated rain will soak the ground and raise river flows, which could matter for later storms. Forecasters are confident in the shift to a wetter, windier pattern from Friday, but less sure how strong Friday's winds will be.
changes: The morning discussion expected the first wet, breezy system Wednesday and the strongest one Thursday night into Friday; later discussions pushed the active pattern back, with a weak front Wednesday evening into Thursday and the stronger storms starting Friday. Later updates also added the weekend power outage risk from leafy trees and gave 40 to 80% odds of gusts over 40 mph for the coast and north of Admiralty Inlet.
